contract.words: Collect $3,000 of settled cash within 30 days using no up-front capital.

terms.proofCondition: $3,000 of settled cash in the owner's account within 30 days

strategy.title: Test-sell the dead-stock and reorder-point analysis at $350, then scale through the cooperative directory
strategy.why: Buyer, channel, demand, volume (380 directory stores), conversion (18 of 200 on this offer), fulfilment (Brain produces the spreadsheet), economics ($5 cost, $0 tied up) and settlement (3 days) are on the card as evidence. The one unestablished link is the price: $350 is only the owner's statement (PERSON, 2026-11-26), not something any buyer has paid. Ten paid orders at $350 ($3,500) reach the $3,000 target; a first offer round to 100 stores measures whether buyers pay $350 before the rest of the directory is offered.

alternatives.title: Treat the $350 owner statement as the price and plan as EXECUTABLE
alternatives.why: Rejected: a price somebody only said is not evidence; no agreement or payment at $350 is recorded.

alternatives.title: Research published prices for inventory analyses first
alternatives.why: A published range for other consultants would not show what these stores pay for this offer; a live offer measures it directly at $0 capital.

answers.resolution: Agreed; price stays UNKNOWN and is what the test decides (OFFER_AND_PRICE).

answers.resolution: Accepted: step s1 now connects sending and invoicing before the first email on day 0.

facts.value: The cooperative's member directory lists 380 independent hardware stores, each with a published email; each reorders stock every week.
Sell An analysis of the store's point-of-sale export naming dead stock and reorder points; delivered in 3 days. to each buyer.
The owner says hardware store owners would pay $350 for the analysis (owner's statement, 2026-11-26).

reviews.reasons: The stance is right: CONDITIONAL on OFFER_AND_PRICE, because $350 is only the owner's statement (PERSON) and no agreement is recorded; every other link is evidenced, fulfilment (Brain-produced spreadsheet) is proved before orders are taken, and passing the proof at its threshold carries the target (5 paid of 100 = 5% -> 5 + 0.05 x 280 = 19 orders x $350 = $6,650 >= $3,000, at $0 capital). Two defects keep it from being actionable as written: (1) the decision rule leaves a gap - stop below 2 paid orders, continue at 5 or more, nothing for 2-4. At 3 paid (3%) the remaining 280 stores yield ~8 more, 11 x $350 = $3,850, which still reaches the target; at 2 (2%) ~7.6 total, $2,660, does not. The rule should be continue at >= 3 (or state what 2-4 means). (2) The ledger settles each payment the day it is collected, but the card says 3 days to usable cash and payment is on delivery: test orders delivered day 4 settle about day 7, the second batch offered day 8, delivered day 11, settles about day 14. The window still holds, but proofDay and settlesDay should reflect the 3-day lag, and the proof 'settled by day 7' is then on the edge.
findings: Recomputed at the evidenced 9% close rate: 100 contacts -> 9 orders; 10 orders x $350 = $3,500 gross, $50 direct cost, net $3,450; 380 stores (weekly buyers) is ample volume.
Threshold check: proof at 5 of 100 (5%) carries the target with the remaining 280 stores (19 orders, $6,650).
Gap: outcomes of 2-4 paid orders have neither stop nor continue; 3 or 4 paid still reach the target, 2 does not.
Ledger settles receipts on the collection day despite the card's 3 days to usable cash; shift settlesDay (day 7 and ~day 14) and proofDay accordingly.
Conversion 18/200 is on this offer but its price is not stated, so it does not confirm $350; the plan correctly treats price as the unknown the test decides (validation.decides OFFER_AND_PRICE).
Executor SEND_A_MESSAGE and ISSUE_AN_INVOICE are NOT_CONNECTED; they must be connected before day 0.

reviews.reasons: Both defects are fixed and the plan is actionable. CONDITIONAL on OFFER_AND_PRICE is right ($350 is only the owner's statement; no agreement recorded). The decision rule now covers every outcome: continue at >= 3 paid of 100, stop at <= 2. Threshold check: 3% -> 3 + 0.03 x 280 = ~11.4 orders, 11 x $350 = $3,850 >= $3,000; 2% -> ~7.6 orders, $2,660 < $3,000, so the cut is in the right place. The ledger now honours the 3-day settlement (test receipts day 7, second batch day 14), proof day 8, and direct costs ($5 each, $50 total) are paid from settled receipts, so no capital. Fulfilment is a Brain-produced spreadsheet (proved) before any order is taken. Volume (380 weekly-reordering stores) is ample.
findings: Recomputed: 10 x $350 = $3,500 gross, $50 cost, net $3,450; second batch offered day 8, delivered by day 11, settled by day 14 of 30.
At the threshold (3%) the margin is ~$850 over target; at the evidenced 9% it is much wider.
Payment is on delivery, so a buyer can decline after delivery; the $5 cost bounds that loss and the test counts only paid orders, which is correct.
Sending and invoicing are to be connected in s1 before the first email (SEND_A_MESSAGE / ISSUE_AN_INVOICE currently NOT_CONNECTED).
